# United States Commuting At A Glance: American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates

Each year, the American Community Survey publishes statistics related to commuting in the United States. The charts below show trends for key commuting estimates. These graphics are sourced from Table S0801, available at data.census.gov.

- Travel Time to Work: Mean Travel Time to Work [< 1.0 MB] 

The mean one-way travel time in 2025 was 27.4 minutes, higher than 27.2 minutes in 2024.
- Travel Time to Work: Percentage of Workers Traveling 60 Minutes or More [<1.0 MB] 

The percentage of workers with a one-way travel time of 60 minutes or more in 2025 was 9.5 percent, higher than 9.3 percent in 2024.
- Means of Transportation to Work: Drove Alone [< 1.0 MB] 

The percentage of workers who drove alone to work in 2025 was 69.8 percent, higher than 69.2 percent in 2024. 
- Means of Transportation to Work: Public Transportation and Worked from Home [< 1.0 MB] 

The percentage of workers who took public transportation to work in 2025 was 3.8 percent, higher than 3.7 percent in 2024. The percentage of workers who worked from home in 2025 was 12.9 percent, lower than 13.3 percent in 2024.

Note

The COVID-19 pandemic posed challenges to collecting ACS data in 2020 and, as a result, the ACS experienced high rates of non-response. To address these concerns, the Census Bureau released “experimental” estimates for the 2020 ACS 1-year data. For this reason, 2020 ACS 1-year estimates are not provided in these figures. For more information on 2020 ACS data, see user note.

The U.S. Census Bureau has reviewed this data product to ensure appropriate access, use, and disclosure avoidance protection of the confidential source data used to produce this product (Data Management System (DMS) number: P-7533841; Disclosure Review Board (DRB) approval number: CBDRB-FY27-DSEP-002).
